errors.quote: A residual has an orthonormal basis $\mathcal B$ (it has a norm-one coordinate vector)
errors.problem: Most residuals contain no coordinate unit vector of F^{(x)3}. For example, the central residual P x F x Q consists of vectors p x f x q, where p or q is a tensor of triple indicators of weight at least 3. One norm-one vector also does not give an orthonormal basis without nondegeneracy. The paper builds a norm-one vector as a tensor of coordinate units chosen outside the relevant supports, uses the nondegeneracy of each residual, and then proves that nondegenerate nonalternating binary spaces have orthonormal bases.

errors.quote: $X$ labels grow from $A\otimes\langle t\rangle$ to $A\otimes F$, $Y$ labels from $B\otimes\langle t\rangle$ to $(P\otimes\langle t\rangle)^\perp_{A\otimes F}$. Next, $A'=A\otimes F$, $P'=P\otimes\langle t\rangle$, $B'=(P')^\perp_{A'}$, so outgoing labels equal next incoming labels.
errors.problem: The factor Q = <t_{a_{j+1}} x ... x t_{a_3}> is silently dropped, so these are not subspaces of the label space F^{(x)3} the page names. As written, the outgoing X label A x F = A' is not equal to the next incoming label A' x <t_{a_{j+1}}>. The paper tensors every label by Q and splits Q = <t_{a_{j+1}}> x Q' to get the match.

This holds only for an increasing edge (V = U perp E). On a decreasing edge, such as the central edge 3->4, the paper negates the right side. The page displays the formula without that case, and recovers it only implicitly through epsilon = +-1 and 'or its inverse'.
